title: Causal chains from gene to phenotype for the fin genes, with a source and an evidence grade on every link
note: Every link was produced by a subagent working under genotype/AGENT_BRIEF.md: nothing from memory, every statement from a document fetched in that run through the logged fetcher, a verbatim quote per source, and an evidence grade of association (expression only), necessity (loss of function), sufficiency (gain of function), mechanism (a pathway step shown experimentally) or hypothesis (proposed, not shown). A grade is about the link it sits on, not the gene. All of it is zebrafish or other proxy-species work: no flying-fish experiment exists. This file was merged and checked by genotype/assemble_chains.py, which upgrades nothing; validation flags travel with the data.
constraint: Every node below the pectoral fin is a zebrafish anatomy (ZFA) term, and every gene link is a zebrafish or medaka record. None of it is flying-fish data. A flying fish's wing is an enlarged pectoral fin.

coverage.metric_note: chain_strength is the WEAKEST grade on a chain and is the honest measure of it: a chain is only as strong as its weakest link. genes_with_a_link_graded_X counts genes with at least one such link anywhere on the chain, which is a much weaker statement.

summary.note: chains_reaching_mechanism counts chains whose gene->molecular_function AND molecular_function->process steps are both graded mechanism: kcnk5b and kcnh2a. slc43a2a reaches only hypothesis at its process step. chains_reaching_sufficiency counts chains whose final cell_or_tissue_effect->phenotype step is graded sufficiency: all three. No chain has a step graded 'missing', but the slc43a2a process step is empty of experiment and is the thread's real hole.

genes.ray_growth_evidence: Not established for apc itself: apc mutants are scored from 36 hpf to Larval:Protruding-mouth, long before lepidotrichia form, and no fetched source reports rays in an apc mutant. Pathway-level evidence that canonical Wnt sets fin RAY SEGMENT length does exist, from other reagents: Bhattacharya 2018 (PMID 30377172, doi 10.1242/dev.166975) reports 'β-catenin activity is required for segment length, and is reduced in both sofb123 mutants and following Smp knockdown in regenerating fins' and 'We further show that blocking canonical Wnt signaling results in a synergistic reduction in segment length in sofb123/+ heterozygotes'; Wehner 2014 (PMID 24485658) reports 'signaling in cells lining the osteoblasts directs osteoblast differentiation' and that 'Wnt signaling regulates epidermal patterning, blastemal cell proliferation, and osteoblast maturation indirectly via secondary signals'. Both are REGENERATION, use cx43/smp or pharmacological Wnt blockade rather than apc, and were read as abstract only. Ray BRANCHING/bifurcation: not established by any fetched source for Wnt or for apc.
genes.development_or_regeneration: apc evidence is entirely DEVELOPMENTAL (16 hpf to about 4 dpf, embryos and larvae). The ray-segment-length evidence quoted above is entirely REGENERATION (adult caudal fin regenerates) and comes from different genes; the two must not be merged.
genes.weakest_link: process->cell_or_tissue_effect in the PECTORAL fin: the apc allele itself was assayed in the median fin fold, and the pectoral fin fold result used the GSK-3beta inhibitor BIO. The apc-specific pectoral chain therefore relies on a pharmacological stand-in plus the ring1b cross-rescue abstract.
gaps: No apc mutant data on fin rays (lepidotrichia) at all - the mutants do not survive to ray-forming stages in any fetched source.
van der Velden 2012 (PMID 22619390) is not in PMC; only the abstract was read, so the apc-ring1b-Fgf rescue cannot be quoted at figure level.

The ZFIN pectoral fin rows for apc come from a Cell paper on intestine (PMID 20850014) and a Nature paper on cardiac valves (PMID 14534590) whose abstracts do not mention fins; only the curated rows support them.

Bhattacharya 2018 full text could not be retrieved (Europe PMC fullTextXML HTTP 500 for PMC6288381; NCBI PMC efetch publisher-blocked), so which Wnt inhibitor was used for the segment-length experiment is unknown from fetched text.
No fetched source reports LiCl or IWR-1 by name in an apc fin experiment.

cross_gene.notes: Morphological correlation only. This is the one place a flying fish was measured, and it argues AGAINST kcnk5b-type signalling being the flying-fish mechanism despite kcnk5b being the best-understood gene of the three.
